name: Cua đá Cù Lao Chàm
summary: Cua đá is the land crab, Gecarcoidea lalandii, and it is not the daily plate. The Hội An World Heritage centre’s 16 September 2025 study says it left the table and became a forest catch for visitors, at a high price with no figure. Đà Nẵng’s reserve decision of 28 May 2026, effective 10 June 2026, allows the catch only from 1 March to 31 July, and only above a set size.
origin: Cham Islands. A forest crab on Tân Hiệp, regulated inside the nature reserve.
taste: The reserve management board’s 3 March 2026 note says the boiled meat is not fishy, and that it is sweet, fragrant, and firm.
howToEat: The 3 March 2026 note says the crab is grilled, or boiled and eaten with salt and pepper, and that a buyer should take only crab with an eco-label, caught in the allowed season.

Quyết định 63/2026/QĐ-UBND, Article 13, sets the carapace at 7 cm or wider, the season from 1 March to 31 July, and the ground as the intertidal rock of the service-administration zone. The strict zone and the restoration zone are closed to the catch. A current price is Check on arrival.
where: Tân Hiệp, inside the season. The 16 September 2025 study names no shop. Out of season, do not order it.
seoTitle: Cua đá Cù Lao Chàm — stone crab in season
seoDescription: Stone crab on Tân Hiệp is a visitor catch from 1 March to 31 July, carapace 7 cm or wider. It is not the daily plate. A price is Check on arrival.
